source.note: Epilepsy: start 300 mg three times a day, maintenance 300-600 mg three times a day; up to 3600 mg/day (2.1, 2.2) = 1200 mg per dose three times daily.

Falls as dose rises: '60%, 47%, 34%, 33%, and 27% following 900, 1200, 2400, 3600, and 4800 mg/day'. Model 0.6 = value at 900 mg/day (300 mg three times daily, the typical dose); the curve does not model this drop.
'elimination half-life is 5 to 7 hours' model = midpoint of the label range (curve value; change if you prefer another)
'apparent volume of distribution ... after 150 mg intravenous administration is 58 +/- 6 L'

source.citation: NEURONTIN (gabapentin) Product Monograph, Pfizer Canada, Health Canada, p. 18 (Absorption)
source.note: US label gives Tmax only for children (2-3 h). Monograph: 'peak plasma concentrations are observed within 2 to 3 hours'. model = midpoint of the label range (curve value; change if you prefer another)
'eliminated from the systemic circulation by renal excretion as unchanged drug'; 'not appreciably metabolized' (fractions are of the absorbed drug).

journey.text: Absorbed from the gut, but the gut can only take up so much: the bigger the dose, the smaller the share absorbed.
Binds to calcium channels on nerve cells, calming overactive nerve signals behind nerve pain and seizures. Exactly how it helps is not fully known.
Not broken down at all: it leaves unchanged in urine.
